sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent: no 'Adasen', no 'Isnag'; irrelevant to this language (kept only because downloaded).

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 2006. On reconstructing the morphosyntax of Proto-Northern Luzon. Philippine Journal of Linguistics 37(2):1-64 (author preprint, ScholarSpace 10125/32994).
sources.note: Only the abstract extracts (font-encoding problem in body); topic is Central Cordilleran noun-phrase markers, not phonology. ScholarSpace full-text search for 'Adasen' returns 0 hits across all of Reid's deposited papers.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid adas1235 (JSON record and reference list).
sources.note: Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist (Gaioni 1989 ethnographic article; Ethnologue 2009); 5 references total, none a grammar, sketch or phonology.

sources.citation: Same item, handwritten field original (5 pp.).
sources.note: Same stress ticks as the typed copy; no legend or notes.

sources.citation: Tordil, Franxes Ghia U. and Ruby May P. Cabael. 2025. Paghahambing sa mga salitang katawagan ng mga Pangkat Etniko ng Abra [A comparative analysis of the terminologies used by the ethnic groups of Abra]. PANTAO: The International Journal of the Humanities and Social Sciences 4(4):7101-7107. doi:10.69651/2022PIJHSS.
sources.note: In Filipino; 57 elicited terms (people/body parts, animals, objects, places) compared with Iloko; notes segmental substitutions in Adasen (Iloko ngipen > Adasen ngipon, kiday > kidoy, katre > katli, ules > ulos, pirak > pilak) and deletions (pus-ong > pos-on, mata > ata). No mention of diin/stress, tone or any suprasegmental.

sources.citation: Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino. 2023-2025. Repositoryo ng mga Wika at Kultura ng Pilipinas: Mga Wika ng Pilipinas (online language profiles, one page per language, based on KWF 'Lingguwistikong Etnograpiya' field documentation 2017-2021 and PSA 2020 census). Manila: KWF. Profiles read: 'Gáddang', 'Áyta Ambalá', 'Átta', 'Alangán Mangyán', 'Itnëg', 'Kalingga', 'Manóbo Agúsan' (all posted 5-6 Dec 2023).
sources.note: sociolinguistic profile only (location by barangay, vitality grade, PSA 2020 population/household counts, classification); no phonology, nothing on stress (diin)

sources.citation: University of the Philippines Diliman, Department of Linguistics, The Katig Collective. c.2022-2023. Language Capsules (web series on endangered Philippine languages; 30 capsules incl. 'Adasen', 'Agta, Dicamay', 'Agta, Mt. Iriga', 'Alangan', 'Ata', 'Atta, Faire').
sources.note: no phonology; states that apart from Wurm's entry in Moseley (ed.) 2007 the only Adasen work online is the SIL 1962-66 Ba-y wordlist (77088); EGIDS 6b, 4,000 speakers

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David, Jason W. Lobel & William Hall. n.d. [ms. c.2020-2022; published 2024 as ch. 7 'Historical linguistics of the Philippines' in A. Adelaar & A. Schapper (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia, OUP]. The History of the Philippine Languages. 44 pp. typescript, zorc.net item 142a.
sources.note: named as a Cagayan Valley (ex-'Northern Cordilleran') language; nothing on stress

sources.citation: del Corro, Anicia. 2014. Tinggian: What if there is no standard dialect? The Bible Translator 65(2):205-221. doi:10.1177/2051677014529565.
sources.note: No prosody. Sec. 4.4 Tables 1-2 give Adasen syntactic markers (subject marker (i)ya, pluralizer diya, goal marker ka, passive actor marker ne, interrogative kad) and five lexical items (udan 'rain', bedeng 'peace pact', bado 'cloth', dalan 'road', beken NEG); the only phonological remark (p.219) is that Inlaud and Binungan lack the 'exotic phonemes' /f v c j/ of Vanao and Falatok. Cites Walton & Walton 2003 '2003 Itneg Survey Report' (SIL Philippines, unpublished) as covering six Tinggian dialects.

sources.citation: Ethnologue, 17th ed. (2013). Adasen [tiu]. SIL International (the Internet Archive 2013).
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Classification N. Cordilleran > Cagayan Valley > Isnag; dialects Eastern and Western Addasen; 'Comprehension of Isnag [isd] 74%'; NT 1990.

sources.citation: Abaya, Digna Jocelyn L., Marciana P. De Vera and Manuel A. Bajet Jr. 2011. Dialects, beliefs and practices of the Tinguians of Abra. JPAIR Multidisciplinary Journal 6:77-89. doi:10.7719/jpair.v6i1.137.
sources.note: No phonology content: a dialect-by-municipality table and ethnographic material (marriage, death practices). Points to Begnalen, N.B. 2009, 'Mapping and Inventory of the Tingguian Ethno-Language', Research Journal, Abra State Institute of Sciences and Technology 7(1) (print, Lagangilang, Abra) for 'phonemic similarity.. across dialects'.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. Change Requests 2006-058 and 2007-053 (tiu: 'Itneg, Adasen' -> 'Adaseng' -> 'Adasen').
sources.note: Naming/administrative only; no linguistic content.

sources.citation: Himes, Ronald S. 1997. Reconstructions in Kalinga-Itneg. Oceanic Linguistics 36(1):102-134.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Accent-marked comparative data for the Itneg varieties of Abra; may cite or include Adasen forms and comment on accent correspondences, though Adasen is classified outside Kalinga-Itneg. Coverage unverified (JSTOR paywall).

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A., P. Mühlhäusler & D. T. Tryon (eds.). 1996. Atlas of Languages of Intercultural Communication in the Pacific, Asia, and the Americas (Trends in Linguistics. Documentation 13). Berlin/New York: Mouton de Gruyter. DOI 10.1515/9783110819724. [held page-text, 1903 PDF pages]
sources.note: No phonology. Sociolinguistic note only: 'L, E Adasen: pass.bil. in Isnag' and bilingualism in Ilocano 'is present with the speakers of L, E Adasen'.

sources.citation: New Tribes Mission. 1990. Ya Baru nga Tulag [Adasen New Testament]. Sanford, FL: New Tribes Mission (YouVersion version 2812 'YBT', distributed by Global Partners; translators identified in a 1991 Summit Christian College yearbook only as 'Mark, his wife Rachel, and Adasen helpers').
sources.note: Scripture text only, no front matter on orthography online. The practical orthography writes a diacritic e̍ (e.g. ne̍, se̍, Je̍su, mawe̍) that distinguishes a vowel quality (the ɨ of the 1962 'Addassɨn' wordlist) rather than stress; no accent marks for stress. Confirms an NTM orthography (and therefore presumably an unpublished phonemic statement) existed by 1990.

sources.citation: Gaioni, Dominic T. 1989. Traditional health care among the Tingyans. Philippine Studies 37:52-70.
sources.note: Ethnographic article (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as an ethnographic work); not opened; not expected to treat phonology.

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1981. Philippine linguistics: the state of the art: 1970-1980. In D. V. Hart (ed.), Philippine Studies: Political Science, Economics, and Linguistics, 212-273. Northern Illinois University Center for Southeast Asian Studies.
sources.note: No mention of Adasen anywhere; used only to verify citations for the list of works to obtain (McFarland 1977 'an excellent source for lexical and grammatical material from the Northern Philippine languages'; Barlaan 1975, 1977 and Vanoverbergh 1972 on Isneg).

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1979. Towards a reconstruction of the pronominal systems of Proto-Cordilleran, Philippines. In Nguyen Dang Liem (ed.), South-East Asian Linguistic Studies 3, 259-275. Pacific Linguistics C-45.
sources.note: No Adasen data; nothing on Adasen stress.

sources.citation: SIL International (Philippines). [1962-1966]. Addassen - Ba-y, Abra Wordlist (1962 Philippine Word List, 304 items, informant Julio Parinas; typed transcription). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 77088. Unpublished data set, CC BY-NC-SA.
sources.note: No prose at all. Stress is transcribed with a raised tick before the stressed syllable on a subset of items, and it falls on both penults ('bagat, bo'sali, na'pit, na'ngisit) and final syllables (ɨ'min, dap'pog, bɨs'sog, bɨg'gi, baŋ'ka, bɨk'kag, kagab'bi) -- i.e. the raw data look like Ilokano/Isnag-type lexically variable penult-vs-final stress, but no rule is stated.

sources.citation: Barlaan, Rodolfo R. 1999. Aspects of focus in Isnag. (LSP Special Monograph Issue.) Manila: Linguistic Society of the Philippines; and Vanoverbergh, Morice. 1972. Isneg-English Vocabulary. Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 11. Honolulu: University Press of Hawaii (introduction).

sources.note: Nearest described relative (Isnag, isna1241; Ethnologue groups Adasen under 'Isnag', 74% comprehension). Would supply the family-internal expectation (contrastive penult/final stress) but is NOT a description of Adasen and cannot stand in for it in the catalog.

sources.citation: McFarland, Curtis D. 1977. Northern Philippine Linguistic Geography. (Study of Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa Monograph Series 9.) Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: First-hand survey of Northern Luzon speech varieties with wordlists and grammatical notes (Reid 1981: 'an excellent source for lexical and grammatical material from the Northern Philippine languages'); 'Adasen' as a language name in the pre-2005 literature most plausibly traces to McFarland 1977/1980. Whether an Adasen sample point is included, and whether accent is transcribed or described, is unverified.

sources.citation: New Tribes Mission (translators unnamed). Materials behind the Adasen New Testament 'Ya Baru nga Tulag' (1990): orthography statement / phonemic write-up / literacy primers for Adasen.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only sustained linguistic work ever done on Adasen (Ethnologue 17: 'NT: 1990'; find.bible lists the NT). NTM teams normally wrote an unpublished phonemic statement before fixing an orthography; if it exists it is the only place an explicit Adasen stress statement is likely to be found.

sources.citation: SIL Philippines, sociolinguistic survey of the Itneg/Tinguian varieties of Abra (c. 2004-2007; unpublished survey report underlying Ethnologue 15-17 'Comprehension of Isnag 74%', the Eastern/Western Addasen dialect split and the 2005 division of Itneg into six languages).
